FARRA:v2p175/r7.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p175/r7.speaker: author
FARRA:v2p175/r7.claim: The reading وأنا اخترتك attaches to نودي; اخترناك is also read, while إنا اخترناك with kasra starts a new sentence.

NAHHAS:v3p33/r11.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p33/r11.speaker: أهل المدينة وأبو عمرو وعاصم والكسائي
NAHHAS:v3p33/r11.claim: These readers read وأنا اخترتك; the remaining Kufans read وإنا اخترناك, with the same meaning.
NAHHAS:v3p33/r11.anchor: قرأ أهل المدينة وأبو عمرو وعاصم والكسائي

NAHHAS:v3p33/r12.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p33/r12.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v3p33/r12.claim: أنا اخترتك better matches the written form and the sequence leading into يا موسى إني أنا ربك.
NAHHAS:v3p33/r12.anchor: وأنا اخترتك ههنا أولى من جهتين إحداهما أنه أشبه بالخط والثانية أنه أولى بنسق الكلام

JISHUMI:v6p4638/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4638/r1.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4638/r1.claim: On the preceding question about divine istiwāʾ, the author says the sounder view of Abū ʿAlī is that it means power; the Kullābī account of an act or attribute called istiwāʾ is unintelligible.
JISHUMI:v6p4638/r1.anchor: وإن كان الأصح ما ذهب إليه أبو علي أن المراد به الاقتدار

JISHUMI:v6p4638/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4638/r7.speaker: حمزة
JISHUMI:v6p4638/r7.claim: Hamzah intensifies “anā” and reads “ikhtarnāka” with nūn and alif for magnification; the others read “ikhtartuka” with singular tāʾ.
JISHUMI:v6p4638/r7.anchor: قرأ حمزة (أنا) بالتشديد. (اخترناك) بالنون والألف على التفخيم

TABRISI:20:9-16/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:9-16/r3.speaker: حمزة
TABRISI:20:9-16/r3.claim: Hamza reads akhtarnāka in the plural and with a shadda; the other readers have akhtartuka in the singular.
TABRISI:20:9-16/r3.anchor: وأنا مشدد مفتوح الهمزة اخترناك على الجمع والباقون لأهله بكسر الهاء وأنا اخترتك على التوحيد

TABRISI:20:9-16#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:9-16#2/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:20:9-16#2/r1.claim: The plural reading is supported by the Qur'an's shift from the singular mention of the Prophet's night journey to the plural We gave Moses the Book.

TABRISI:20:9-16#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:9-16#2/r2.speaker: أبو علي
TABRISI:20:9-16#2/r2.claim: Hamza's plural form can be parsed as wa-li-annā ikhtarnāka, with the prepositional phrase functioning as the object of fastamiʿ.
TABRISI:20:9-16#2/r2.anchor: أن يكون التقدير ولأنا اخترناك فاستمع فيكون الجار والمجرور في موضع نصب بقوله فاستمع

THALABI:v6p239#2/r9.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p239#2/r9.speaker: حمزة
THALABI:v6p239#2/r9.claim: Hamza reads ‘We have chosen you’ in the plural of majesty; اخترتك means ‘I selected you.’
THALABI:v6p239#2/r9.anchor: وأنا اخترتك اصطفيتك، وقرأ حمزة: وإنا اخترناك بلفظ الجمع على التعظيم

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:9-14/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:9-14/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:9-14/r4.claim: God chose Moses for prophethood and told him to listen to the revelation.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p18/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p18/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p18/r2.claim: The command to listen attentively focuses Moses before the revelation and marks both his honor and new responsibility.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p18/r2.anchor: This sentence is meant to focus the attention of Moses (sws)

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p18/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p18/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p18/r3.claim: Appointment as God’s messenger brought Moses honor and respect along with a great responsibility.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p18/r3.anchor: Evident from this verse is the honour and respect

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p316/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p316/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p316/r6.claim: Some read a first-person plural “We chose you”; the majority has singular “I chose you,” with royal-plural and Ubayy’s yāʾ readings also reported.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p316/r6.anchor: والجمهور وأنا اخترتك بضمير المتكلم المفرد غير المعظم نفسه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p316/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p316/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p316/r7.claim: Lima yūḥā is most naturally attached to istamiʿ and means “that which is revealed”; attachment to ikhtartuka is rejected by the two-governor rule.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p316/r7.anchor: والظاهر أن لما يوحى من صلة استمع وما بمعنى الذي

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p317/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p317/r1.speaker: أبو الفضل الجوهري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p317/r1.claim: Al-Jawharī describes Moses standing and leaning on a stone, hands folded and chin lowered, listening in wool clothes.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p317/r1.anchor: وقف على حجر واستند إلى حجر ووضع يمينه على شماله

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p317/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p317/r2.speaker: وهب
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p317/r2.claim: Wahb defines proper listening as still limbs, lowered gaze, attentive hearing, present mind, and resolve to act.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p317/r2.anchor: أدب الاستماع سكون الجوارح وغض البصر والإصغاء بالسمع

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p317/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p317/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p317/r3.claim: The passive yuḥā suppresses its known agent and suits the verse ending; the revelation is God’s declaration of exclusive divinity.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p317/r3.anchor: وحذف الفاعل في يوحى للعلم به ويحسنه كونه فاصلة

BIQAI-FULL:v5p13/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p13/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p13/r8.claim: God chose Moses as a prophet and instructed him to listen with focused attention; the private, intimate-sounding address signals his honor even though it is heard openly.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p13/r8.anchor: أي أنصت ملقيا سمعك معملا قلبك للسماع

STUDYQURAN:20:13/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:20:13/r1.speaker: R
STUDYQURAN:20:13/r1.claim: God’s choosing Moses means conferring messengerhood and the special distinction of direct address, hence his title Kalīm Allāh.

STUDYQURAN:20:13/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:20:13/r2.speaker: Abū Sulaymān al-Dārānī
STUDYQURAN:20:13/r2.claim: Al-Dārānī says God found Moses’ heart the most humble among Adam’s children and therefore singled him out for direct speech.
STUDYQURAN:20:13/r2.anchor: According to the early Sufi figure Abū Sulaymān al-Dārānī

TABATABAI:20:11-14/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:11-14/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:20:11-14/r4.claim: Other passages place a veil or intermediary in Moses' call; this is compatible with revelation, since the message is experienced as God's when attention passes over the unseen mediator.
TABATABAI:20:11-14/r4.anchor: فإن التفت إلى الواسطة التي تحمل الكلام واحتجب بها عنه تعالى كان الكلام رسالة أرسل إليه بملك مثلا

TABATABAI:20:13-14/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:13-14/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:20:13-14/r2.claim: Choosing derives from خير: an agent weighs alternatives and selects the best for a purpose; God chose Moses as best suited to receive prophecy and mission.
TABATABAI:20:13-14/r2.anchor: وحقيقته أن يتردد أمر الفاعل مثلا بين أفعال يجب أن يرجح واحدا منها ليفعله فيميز ما هو خيرها

TABATABAI:20:13-14/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:13-14/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:20:13-14/r3.claim: In context, 'I chose you' performs the conferral of prophecy and mission rather than reporting an earlier choice; the command to listen follows from it.
TABATABAI:20:13-14/r3.anchor: على ما يعطيه السياق من قبيل إصدار الأمر بنبوته ورسالته فهو إنشاء لا إخبار

TABATABAI:20:13-14/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:13-14/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:20:13-14/r4.claim: Listening to what is revealed means attending closely to it.

TABATABAI:20:13-14/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:13-14/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:20:13-14/r5.claim: The following eleven verses include prophecy and mission: prophecy is stated first, while the mission begins with Moses' staff question and ends with the order to go to Pharaoh; Moses is called both prophet and messenger elsewhere.
TABATABAI:20:13-14/r5.anchor: هذا هو الوحي الذي أمر عليه السلام بالاستماع له في إحدى عشرة آية تشتمل على النبوة والرسالة معا

TABRISI:20:12-14/r14.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:12-14/r14.speaker: author
TABRISI:20:12-14/r14.claim: God chose Moses for the prophetic mission and told him to listen carefully and steadily to the revelation; after announcing his prophethood, He instructed him to hear the revelation.
TABRISI:20:12-14/r14.anchor: إليك من كلامي واصغ إليه وتثبت

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p371/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p371/r1.speaker: الكلبي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p371/r1.claim: Al-Kalbī says God chose Moses for His message so that Moses would carry out His command.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p371/r1.anchor: قال الكلبي: (أنا اخترتك برسالتي لكي تقوم بأمري)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p371/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p371/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p371/r2.claim: Listening to the revelation means acting on what God commands and forbids.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p371/r2.anchor: {فاستمع لما يوحى} أي: اعمل بما آمرك به وأنهاك عنه.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p254/r6.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p254/r6.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p254/r6.claim: God chose Moses for His message and speech.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p254/r7.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p254/r7.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p254/r7.claim: Moses is to listen to what is revealed to him.

QASHANI:20:12-13/r5.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:20:12-13/r5.speaker: author
QASHANI:20:12-13/r5.claim: The choice follows complete self-disclosure: Moses' mountain-like existence crumbled in annihilation, and he fell stunned before awakening through true existence.
QASHANI:20:12-13/r5.anchor: هذا وعد بالاصطفاء الذي كان بعد التجلي التام الذاتي الذي جعل جبل وجوده دكا بالفناء فيه بالاندكاك

QASHANI:20:12-13/r6.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:20:12-13/r6.speaker: author
QASHANI:20:12-13/r6.claim: This is disclosure of attributes before Essence; Moses is sent without prophetic commissioning by revelation at this point, and is ordered to spiritual discipline, presence, and vigilance.
QASHANI:20:12-13/r6.anchor: وهذا التجلي هو تجلي الصفات قبل تجلي الذات، ولهذا أرسله ولم يستنبئه بالوحي هنا

QASHANI:20:12-13/r7.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:20:12-13/r7.speaker: author
QASHANI:20:12-13/r7.claim: This choice is near the original election in 20:122, intermediate between that election and the later selection.
QASHANI:20:12-13/r7.anchor: فهذا الاختيار قريب من الاجتباء الأصلي المشار إليه بقوله:

QUSHAYRI:v2p255/r4.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p255/r4.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p255/r4.claim: God's choice, made with knowledge of Moses, strips and purifies him of illusions and whatever clouds his clarity.
QUSHAYRI:v2p255/r4.anchor: وعلى علم مني بك اصطفيتك ، وجردتك ونقيتك عن دنس الأوهام وكل ما يكدر صفوك

QUSHAYRI:v2p255/r5.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p255/r5.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p255/r5.claim: After being chosen, Moses belongs to God and acts through Him, effaced from himself in annihilation.
QUSHAYRI:v2p255/r5.anchor: ويقال بعدما اخترتك فأنت لي وبي ، وأنت محو في فنائك عنك

SULAMI:v1p437#2/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p437#2/r1.speaker: الواسطي
SULAMI:v1p437#2/r1.claim: God's chosen servant is nurtured and selected, loved by God's servants, enabled to speak clearly, and given ease in his affairs so he can stand firm before revelation.
SULAMI:v1p437#2/r1.anchor: قول الواسطي : المختار من جهته من هو مصطنعه ومصطفيه ،

SAMIN-DURR:20:13/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:13/r1.speaker: حمزة في آخرين
SAMIN-DURR:20:13/r1.claim: Hamza and other readers use the plural-form اخترناك with an open hamza and the first-person plural of majesty.
SAMIN-DURR:20:13/r1.anchor: قرأ حمزة في آخرين " وأنا اخترناك " بفتح الهمزة بضمير المتكلم المعظم نفسه.

SAMIN-DURR:20:13/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:13/r2.speaker: السلمي والأعمش وابن هرمز
SAMIN-DURR:20:13/r2.claim: Al-Sulami, al-Aʿmash, and Ibn Hurmuz also read اخترناك, but with kasra on the hamza.
SAMIN-DURR:20:13/r2.anchor: وقرأ السلمي والأعمش وابن هرمز كذلك، إلا أنهم كسروا الهمزة.

SAMIN-DURR:20:13/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:13/r3.speaker: الباقون
SAMIN-DURR:20:13/r3.claim: The remaining readers use the singular first-person form اخترتك.
SAMIN-DURR:20:13/r3.anchor: والباقون " وأنا اخترتك " بضمير المتكلم وحده.

SAMIN-DURR:20:13/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:13/r4.speaker: أبي
SAMIN-DURR:20:13/r4.claim: Ubayy reads وأني اخترتك with fatḥa on the hamza.
SAMIN-DURR:20:13/r4.anchor: وقرأ أبي " وأني اخترتك " بفتح الهمزة.

SAMIN-DURR:20:13/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:13/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:20:13/r5.claim: Hamza's open hamza coordinates with إني أنا ربك read open; readers of the kasra form coordinate with its kasra, and Ubayy's reading follows Hamza's coordination.
SAMIN-DURR:20:13/r5.anchor: فأما قراءة حمزة فعطف على قوله { إني أنا ربك } ، وذلك أنه بفتح الهمزة هناك،

SAMIN-DURR:20:13/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:13/r6.speaker: أبو البقاء
SAMIN-DURR:20:13/r6.claim: Abu al-Baqa allows the open hamza to mean 'because I chose you, so listen,' attaching the clause to استمع.
SAMIN-DURR:20:13/r6.anchor: وجوز أبو البقاء أن يكون الفتح على تقدير: ولأنا اخترناك فاستمع، فعلقه باستمع.

SAMIN-DURR:20:13/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:13/r7.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:20:13/r7.claim: The author prefers coordinating the reading with the preceding إني أنا ربك.

SAMIN-DURR:20:13/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:13/r8.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:20:13/r8.claim: The second object of اخترتك is omitted; the sense is 'I chose you from among your people.'
SAMIN-DURR:20:13/r8.anchor: ومفعول " اخترتك " الثاني محذوف أي: اخترتك من قومك.

SAMIN-DURR:20:13/r9.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:13/r9.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:20:13/r9.claim: The apparent construction attaches لما يوحى to استمع.
SAMIN-DURR:20:13/r9.anchor: قوله { لما يوحى } الظاهر تعلقه ب " استمع ".

SAMIN-DURR:20:13/r10.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:13/r10.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:20:13/r10.claim: The lām may be extra before the object, as in 27:72.
SAMIN-DURR:20:13/r10.anchor: ويجوز أن تكون اللام مزيدة في المفعول على حد قوله تعالى: ردف لكم

SAMIN-DURR:20:13/r11.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:13/r11.speaker: الزمخشري وغيره
SAMIN-DURR:20:13/r11.claim: Al-Zamakhshari and others see تنازع between اخترتك and استمع: Moses was chosen for revelation and must listen to that revelation.
SAMIN-DURR:20:13/r11.anchor: وجوز الزمخشري وغيره أن تكون المسألة من باب التنازع بين " اخترتك " وبين " استمع "

SAMIN-DURR:20:13/r12.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:13/r12.speaker: الشيخ
SAMIN-DURR:20:13/r12.claim: The Sheikh argues that technical attachment to اخترتك would require repeating the pronoun with the second verb, so the construction is governed by the second verb.
SAMIN-DURR:20:13/r12.anchor: وقد رد الشيخ هذا بأن قال: " ولا يجوز التعليق ب " اخترتك " لأنه من باب الإعمال، يجب أو يختار إعادة الضمير مع الثاني

SAMIN-DURR:20:13/r13.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:13/r13.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:20:13/r13.claim: The author clarifies that al-Zamakhshari meant semantic suitability, not technical grammatical government.
SAMIN-DURR:20:13/r13.anchor: قلت: الزمخشري عنى التعليق المعنوي من حيث الصلاحية، وأما تقدير الصناعة فلم يعنه.

SAMIN-DURR:20:13/r14.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:13/r14.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:20:13/r14.claim: ما can be a verbal noun, meaning revelation, or a relative pronoun, meaning that which is revealed.
SAMIN-DURR:20:13/r14.anchor: و " ما " يجوز أن تكون مصدرية، وبمعنى الذي أي: فاستمع للوحي أو للذي يوحى.

ZAJJAJ:v3p351/r6.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p351/r6.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p351/r6.claim: Another reading is wa-anā ikhtarnāka, We chose you.

ZAJJAJ:v3p351/r7.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p351/r7.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p351/r7.claim: For wa-innā ikhtarnāka, the initial clause may be a resumption or quoted speech, reporting that Moses was told, We chose you.
ZAJJAJ:v3p351/r7.anchor: ويجوز (وإنا اخترناك) على وجهين: على الاستئناف

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p221/r1.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p221/r1.speaker: ابن كثير ونافع وأبو عمرو وعاصم وابن عامر والكسائي
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p221/r1.claim: These readers use the singular ‘I chose you,’ with a light nūn and no alif in the verb.
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p221/r1.anchor: فقرأ ابن كثير ونافع وأبو عمرو وعاصم وابن عامر والكسائي: وأنا خفيف اخترتك بالتاء بغير ألف.

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p221/r2.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p221/r2.speaker: حمزة
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p221/r2.claim: Hamza reads the nūn with tashdīd and the verb in the plural form, اخترناك.
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p221/r2.anchor: وقرأ حمزة (وأنا) النون مشددة (اخترناك) بألف ونون

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p221/r3.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p221/r3.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p221/r3.claim: Al-Farisi prefers the singular because it matches ‘I am your Lord’; the plural has a Qurʾanic parallel in 17:1–2, but reports of Ubayy’s reading strengthen the singular.
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p221/r3.anchor: قال أبو علي: الإفراد زعموا أكثر في القراءة، وهو أشبه بما قبله من قوله: إني أنا ربك

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p221/r4.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p221/r4.speaker: الأعمش وأبي
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p221/r4.claim: The plural is reported for al-Aʿmash, while Ubayy’s codex is reported to have wa-annī ikhtartuka, supporting the singular reading.
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p221/r4.anchor: وزعموا أنه قراءة الأعمش، وزعموا أنه في حرف أبي: (وأني اخترتك) فهذا يقوي الوجه الأول.

IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p240#2/r1.author: Ibn Khālawayh (attr.)
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p240#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p240#2/r1.claim: With light “anā,” open hamza, and singular “ikhtartuka,” anā is the subject, ikhtartu its predicate, tāʾ the agent, and ka the object.
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p240#2/r1.anchor: فالحجة لمن فتح الهمزة وخفف وأتى بالتاء أنه جعل أنا اسما لله تعالى مقدما

IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p240#2/r2.author: Ibn Khālawayh (attr.)
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p240#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p240#2/r2.claim: The kasra and doubled-nūn reading treats innī as an accusative particle beginning a clause; its nūn is doubled from two assimilated nūns.
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p240#2/r2.anchor: والحجة لمن كسر الهمزة وشدد النون أنه جعلها حرفا ناصبا مبتدأ وشدد النون لأنها في الأصل نونان أدغمت

IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p240#2/r3.author: Ibn Khālawayh (attr.)
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p240#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p240#2/r3.claim: With open hamza and first-person plural “ikhtarnāka,” the clause continues “innī anā rabbuka”; the plural is the royal we used by rulers.
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p240#2/r3.anchor: والحجة لمن فتحها أنه رد الكلام على قوله

IBNMUJAHID:v1p417/r1.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p417/r1.speaker: ابن كثير ونافع وعاصم وأبو عمرو وابن عامر والكسائي
IBNMUJAHID:v1p417/r1.claim: These readers use light nūn in وأنا and اخترتك with tāʾ and no added alif; Hamza reads doubled nūn and اخترناك with alif and nūn.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p417/r1.anchor: فقرأ ابن كثير ونافع وعاصم وأبو عمرو وابن عامر والكسائى ﴿ وإنا ﴾ خفيفة النون ﴿ اخترتك ﴾ بالتاء بغير ألف

IBNMUJAHID:v1p417/r2.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p417/r2.speaker: حمزة
IBNMUJAHID:v1p417/r2.claim: Hamza reads وإنا with doubled nūn and اخترناك with alif and nūn.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p417/r2.anchor: وقرأ حمزة ﴿ وإنا ﴾ بالنون مشددة / اخترنك / بألف ونون

NASHR:v2p319#2/r3.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p319#2/r3.speaker: حمزة
NASHR:v2p319#2/r3.claim: Hamza reads وأنا as أناّ and اخترتك as اخترناك, using a plural form; the other readers use light nūn and the singular اخترتك.
NASHR:v2p319#2/r3.anchor: النون مفتوحة وألف بعدها على لفظ الجمع

NASHR:v2p322/r10.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p322/r10.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p322/r10.claim: By Abu Ja'far's general rule, the yāʾs should be open where he cuts the hamza, but Ibn al-Jazari found no explicit transmission for that inference.
NASHR:v2p322/r10.anchor: مذهب أبي جعفر فتحها لمن قطع الهمزة عنه، ولكني لم أجده منصوصا

QIRAAT-ER:20:13:2#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:20:13:2#1/r1.speaker: Gm
QIRAAT-ER:20:13:2#1/r1.claim: Reading anna makes the clause subordinate to the preceding verb, meaning and that I chose you.
QIRAAT-ER:20:13:2#1/r1.anchor: Reading with anna (intensifying particle + first-person) instead of ana (pronoun): changes syntactic structure

QIRAAT-ER:20:13:3#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:20:13:3#1/r1.speaker: Pf|Dot
QIRAAT-ER:20:13:3#1/r1.claim: The variant uses the first person plural We have chosen instead of singular I chose, shifting from intimate singular address to majestic divine plural.
QIRAAT-ER:20:13:3#1/r1.anchor: Canonical variant with 1st person plural -nā instead of singular -tu: ""We have chosen you"" — majestic plural vs singular divine ""I""

ALUSI-FULL:v16p170/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p170/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p170/r1.claim: God selected Moses from humanity, or specifically from his people, for prophethood and messengership.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p170/r1.anchor: أي اصطفيتك من الناس أو من قومك للنبوة والرسالة

ALUSI-FULL:v16p170/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p170/r2.speaker: السلمي وابن هرمز والأعمش
ALUSI-FULL:v16p170/r2.claim: Al-Sulami, Ibn Harmuz, and one transmission from al-Aʿmash read wa-annī with kasra and a doubled nūn, and اخترناك with a plural subject.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p170/r2.anchor: وقرأ السلمى وابن هرمز والأعمش في رواية ( وانا ) بكسر الهمزة

ALUSI-FULL:v16p170/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p170/r3.speaker: طلحة وابن أبي ليلى وحمزة وخلف والأعمش
ALUSI-FULL:v16p170/r3.claim: Talha, Ibn Abi Layla, Hamza, Khalaf, and another transmission from al-Aʿmash read the plural اخترناك with fatḥa on أن, supplying أعلم.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p170/r3.anchor: وكذا قرأ طلحة وابن أبى ليلى وحمزة وخلف والأعمش في روايا اخرى إلا انهم فتحوا همزة ان

ALUSI-FULL:v16p170/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p170/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p170/r4.claim: One analysis connects this clause to the preceding command to remove the sandals; with the earlier fatḥa reading, it may instead coordinate with أني أنا ربك whether attached to نودي or implied أعلم.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p170/r4.anchor: وهو على ما قيل عطف على ( اخلع ) ويجوز عند من قرأ ( انى انا ربك ) بالفتح

ALUSI-FULL:v16p170/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p170/r5.speaker: أبو البقاء
ALUSI-FULL:v16p170/r5.claim: Abu al-Baqa suggests an implied lām: because God selected Moses, he should listen to what is revealed; al-Alusi dismisses the analysis.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p170/r5.anchor: وجوز أبو البقاء أن يكون بتقدير اللام وهو متعلق بما بعده أي لانا اخترناك

ALUSI-FULL:v16p170/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p170/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p170/r6.claim: The ف makes the command to listen follow from Moses' selection, which provides the reason for listening.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p170/r6.anchor: والفاء في قوله تعالى ( فاستمع ) لترتيب الأمر والمامور به

ALUSI-FULL:v16p170/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p170/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p170/r7.claim: The lām in لما يوحى attaches to استمع; a proposed attachment to اخترناك is rejected by Abu Hayyan as problematic coordination.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p170/r7.anchor: وجوز أن تكون متعلقة باخترناك ورده أبو حيان

ALUSI-FULL:v16p170/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p170/r8.speaker: أبو حيان
ALUSI-FULL:v16p170/r8.claim: Abu Hayyan says attaching the lām to اخترناك creates an ʿamal construction that should repeat the pronoun, as in فاستمع له لما يوحى; the reply allows either attachment by alternative coordination.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p170/r8.anchor: بأنه يكون حينئذ من باب الاعمال ويجب أو يختار حينئذ اعادة الضمير مع الثانى

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p267#2/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p267#2/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p267#2/r1.claim: God chose Moses and selected him for His messages.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p267#2/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p267#2/r2.speaker: حمزة
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p267#2/r2.claim: Hamza intensifies the nūn in anā and reads ikhtarnā, using the plural of majesty.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p267#2/r2.anchor: قرأ حمزة: "وأنا " مشددة النون، "اخترناك" على التعظيم.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p267#2/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p267#2/r3.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p267#2/r3.claim: Moses is commanded to listen to what is revealed to him.

BAYDAWI-FULL:20:13-14/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:13-14/r2.speaker: حمزة
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:13-14/r2.claim: Ḥamza reads وإنا اخترناك with plural suffix and a different initial form.

BAYDAWI-FULL:20:13-14/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:13-14/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:13-14/r3.claim: Moses is to listen to what is revealed, meaning either the content revealed to him or the revelation itself.

BAYDAWI-FULL:20:13-14/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:13-14/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:13-14/r4.claim: The lām may attach to either of the two preceding verbs.
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:13-14/r4.anchor: واللام تحتمل التعلق بكل من الفعلين

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p39/r12.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p39/r12.speaker: السبعة غير حمزة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p39/r12.claim: The seven readers other than Hamza read وأنا اخترتك; the wording harmonizes with وأنا ربك.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p39/r12.anchor: وقرأ السبعة غير حمزة «وأنا اخترتك» ويؤيد هذه القراءة تناسبها مع قوله أنا ربك

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p39/r13.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p39/r13.speaker: أبي بن كعب
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p39/r13.claim: Ubayy ibn Kaʿb's codex reads وأني اخترتك.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p39/r13.anchor: وفي مصحف أبي بن كعب «وأني اخترتك»

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p39/r14.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p39/r14.speaker: حمزة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p39/r14.claim: Hamza reads وأنا اخترناك in the plural, with a fatḥa on the hamza and a doubled nūn; Ibn Atiyya compares a singular-to-plural shift at 17:1–2.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p39/r14.anchor: وقرأ حمزة «وأنا اخترناك» بالجمع وفتح الهمزة وشد النون، والآية على هذا بمنزلة قوله

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p39/r15.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p39/r15.speaker: فرقة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p39/r15.claim: One group reads وإنا اخترناك with kasra on the initial hamza.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p39/r15.anchor: وقرأت فرقة وإنا اخترناك» يكسر الألف

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p39/r16.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p39/r16.speaker: أبو الفضل بن الجوهري
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p39/r16.claim: Al-Jawhari describes Moses listening while standing against a stone, right hand over left, chin lowered, and dressed entirely in wool.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p39/r16.anchor: سمعت أبا الفضل بن الجوهري يقول: لما قيل لموسى فاستمع وقف على حجر، واستند إلى حجر

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p275/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p275/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p275/r1.anchor: قوله تعالى وأنا اخترتك أي اصطفيتك

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p275/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p275/r2.speaker: حمزة والمفضل
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p275/r2.claim: Hamza and al-Mufaḍḍal read with a doubled nūn and an alif in ikhtarnāka.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p275/r2.anchor: وقرأ حمزة والمفضل وأنا بالنون المشددة اخترناك بألف

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p275/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p275/r3.speaker: ابن الأنباري
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p275/r3.claim: Ibn al-Anbari says “listen” here means to be silent and attentive to the revelation.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p275/r3.anchor: قال ابن الأنباري الاستماع هاهنا محمول على الإنصات المعنى فأنصت لوحيي

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p275/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p275/r4.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p275/r4.claim: The revelation to which Moses must listen is “I am God; there is no god but Me, so worship Me.”
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p275/r4.anchor: والوحي هاهنا قوله إنني أنا الله لا إله إلا أنا فاعبدني

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p277/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p277/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p277/r1.claim: God chose Moses above all people alive in his time through prophethood and speech, as in the statement that He selected him above the people by His messages and words.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p277/r1.anchor: وقوله: {وأنا اخترتك} كقوله {إني اصطفيتك على الناس برسالاتي وبكلامي} [الأعراف: 144] أي:

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p277/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p277/r2.speaker: قيل
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p277/r2.claim: An unnamed report has God ask Moses why He singled him out for speech; Moses says he does not know, and God answers that no one had humbled himself before Him as Moses did.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p277/r2.anchor: قيل: إن الله تعالى قال: يا موسى، أتدري لم خصصتك بالتكليم من بين الناس؟

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p277/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p277/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p277/r3.claim: God tells Moses to listen now to what He is saying and revealing to him.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p277/r3.anchor: {فاستمع لما يوحى} أي: اسمع الآن ما أقول لك وأوحيه إليك

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p56#2/r17.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p56#2/r17.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p56#2/r17.claim: لما يوحى can mean what is revealed or revelation itself, and its preposition can attach either to استمع or اخترتك.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p56#2/r17.anchor: { لما يوحى } للذي يوحى . أو للوحي . تعلق اللام باستمع ، أو باخترتك

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p395/r13.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p395/r13.speaker: مجاهد
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p395/r13.claim: Mujahid interprets establishing prayer for God's remembrance as remembering Him during prayer.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p395/r13.anchor: وأقم الصلاة لتذكرني فيها , قاله مجاهد

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p395/r14.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p395/r14.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p395/r14.claim: Another interpretation is to establish prayer by remembering God, since one enters prayer only through His remembrance.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p395/r14.anchor: وأقم الصلاة بذكري , لأنه لا يدخل في الصلاة إلا بذكره

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p395/r15.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p395/r15.speaker: إبراهيم
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p395/r15.claim: Ibrahim interprets the phrase as praying when one remembers the prayer.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p395/r15.anchor: وأقم الصلاة حين تذكرها , قاله إبراهيم

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p395/r16.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p395/r16.speaker: سعيد بن المسيب
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p395/r16.claim: Saʿid ibn al-Musayyib reports that the Prophet said whoever forgets a prayer should perform it when he remembers.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p395/r16.anchor: وروى سعيد بن المسيب أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال : ( من نسي صلاة فليصلها إذا ذكرها )

MUQATIL:20:13-15/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:20:13-15/r1.speaker: author
MUQATIL:20:13-15/r1.claim: God chose Moses as a messenger and tells him to listen to what is revealed to him, namely God's declaration of His oneness.
MUQATIL:20:13-15/r1.anchor: يا موسى للرسالة { فاستمع لما يوحى

MUQATIL:20:13-15/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:20:13-15/r2.speaker: كعب
MUQATIL:20:13-15/r2.claim: Ka'b reports that God spoke to Moses twice, Muhammad saw his Lord twice, and Adam disobeyed his Lord twice; Muqatil gives no grading.
MUQATIL:20:13-15/r2.anchor: عن كعب: أن موسى، عليه السلام، كلمه ربه مرتين

MUQATIL:20:13-15/r3.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:20:13-15/r3.speaker: عبد الحميد بن يوسف
MUQATIL:20:13-15/r3.claim: Abd al-Hamid b. Yusuf says the cry of a partridge is the words The Merciful rose over the Throne; Muqatil gives no grading.
MUQATIL:20:13-15/r3.anchor: عن عبد الحميد بن يوسف، قال صياح الدراج

NASAFI-FULL:v3p51#6/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p51#6/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p51#6/r1.claim: God chose Moses, selecting him for prophethood.

NASAFI-FULL:v3p51#6/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p51#6/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p51#6/r2.claim: Ḥamza reads the plural “We chose you”; other readers have singular “I chose you.”

NASAFI-FULL:v3p51#6/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p51#6/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p51#6/r3.claim: Moses is to listen to what is revealed or to the revelation itself.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p51#6/r3.anchor: ﴿ فاستمع لما يوحى ﴾ اليك للذي يوحى أو للوحي

NASAFI-FULL:v3p51#6/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p51#6/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p51#6/r4.claim: The lām can attach to istamiʿ or, alternatively, ikhtartuka.

QURTUBI-FULL:20:12-13/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:12-13/r12.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:20:12-13/r12.claim: God selected Moses for the prophetic mission.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:12-13/r12.anchor: قوله تعالى: { وأنا اخترتك } أي اصطفيتك للرسالة.

QURTUBI-FULL:20:12-13/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:12-13/r13.speaker: أهل المدينة وأبو عمرو وعاصم والكسائي
QURTUBI-FULL:20:12-13/r13.claim: The readers of Madina, Abū ʿAmr, ʿĀṣim, and al-Kisāʾī read اخترتك in the singular.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:12-13/r13.anchor: وقرأ أهل المدينة وأبو عمرو وعاصم والكسائي { وأنا اخترتك }.

QURTUBI-FULL:20:12-13/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:12-13/r14.speaker: حمزة
QURTUBI-FULL:20:12-13/r14.claim: Ḥamza reads اخترناك in the plural; the sense is the same, but Qurṭubī prefers singular for the rasm and flow of direct address.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:12-13/r14.anchor: وقرأ حمزة «وأنا اخترناك». والمعنى واحد إلا أن { وأنا اخترتك } ها هنا أولى

QURTUBI-FULL:20:12-13/r15.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:12-13/r15.speaker: النحاس
QURTUBI-FULL:20:12-13/r15.claim: Al-Naḥḥās gives reasons to prefer the singular: it better fits the written form and the direct address to Moses.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:12-13/r15.anchor: والثانية: أنها أولى بنسق الكلام لقوله عز وجل: { يموسى إني أنا ربك فاخلع نعليك } وعلى هذا النسق جرت المخاطبة قاله النحاس.

QURTUBI-FULL:20:12-13/r16.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:12-13/r16.speaker: أبو الفضل الجوهري
QURTUBI-FULL:20:12-13/r16.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya reports his father quoting Abū al-Faḍl al-Jawharī: Moses stood by a stone, leaned on one, folded his hands, lowered his chin, and listened, wearing wool.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:12-13/r16.anchor: سمعت أبا الفضل الجوهري رحمه الله تعالى يقول: لما قيل لموسى صلوات الله وسلامه عليه:

QURTUBI-FULL:20:13-14/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:13-14/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:20:13-14/r1.claim: Qurṭubī praises attentive listening, citing those who follow the best words, a warning about how some listen, and the command to listen silently to Qurʾān.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:13-14/r1.anchor: الذين يستمعون القول فيتبعون أحسنه أولئك الذين هداهم الله

QURTUBI-FULL:20:13-14/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:13-14/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:20:13-14/r2.claim: God commands attentive listening as a discipline, since it brings understanding from Him.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:13-14/r2.anchor: وقال ها هنا: { فاستمع لما يوحى } لأن بذلك ينال الفهم عن الله تعالى.

QURTUBI-FULL:20:13-14/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:13-14/r3.speaker: وهب بن منبه
QURTUBI-FULL:20:13-14/r3.claim: Wahb defines good listening as still limbs, lowered gaze, attentive hearing, present mind, and resolve to understand and act.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:13-14/r3.anchor: روي عن وهب بن منبه أنه قال: من أدب الاستماع سكون الجوارح وغض البصر، والإصغاء بالسمع،

QURTUBI-FULL:20:13-14/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:13-14/r4.speaker: سفيان بن عيينة
QURTUBI-FULL:20:13-14/r4.claim: Sufyān orders learning as listening, understanding, memorizing, acting, and teaching; sincere listening to revelation brings understanding and light in the heart.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:13-14/r4.anchor: وقال سفيان بن عيينة: أول العلم الاستماع، ثم الفهم، ثم الحفظ، ثم العمل، ثم النشر

BURSEVI:v5p285/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p285/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p285/r6.claim: God chose Moses, selecting him for prophethood and messengership.

BURSEVI:v5p285/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p285/r7.speaker: حمزة
BURSEVI:v5p285/r7.claim: Ḥamza reads the verb in the plural form, “We chose you,” instead of “I chose you.”

BURSEVI:v5p285/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p285/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p285/r8.claim: Moses is told to listen attentively to the command and prohibition revealed by God.
BURSEVI:v5p285/r8.anchor: للذي يوحى إليك مني من الأمر والنهي

BURSEVI:v5p285/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p285/r9.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p285/r9.claim: The lām is attached to the verb of hearing as an added preposition before its object, as in “radifa lakum.”
BURSEVI:v5p285/r9.anchor: اللام متعلقة بالسمع مزيدة في المفعول كما في ردف لكم

RAZI-FULL:v22p17#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p17#2/r1.speaker: حمزة وأبي بن كعب
RAZI-FULL:v22p17#2/r1.claim: Ḥamza reads وإنا اخترناك; Ubayy ibn Kaʿb reads وإني اخترتك here.
RAZI-FULL:v22p17#2/r1.anchor: قرأ حمزة : ( وإنا اخترناك ) وقرأ أبي بن كعب : ( وإني اخترتك ) ههنا

RAZI-FULL:v22p17#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p17#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p17#2/r2.claim: God chose Moses for prophethood and privileged speech; this shows prophethood comes through God’s initial choice, not human entitlement.
RAZI-FULL:v22p17#2/r2.anchor: معناه اخترتك للرسالة وللكلام الذي خصصتك به ، وهذه الآية تدل على أن النبوة لا تحصل بالاستحقاق

RAZI-FULL:v22p17#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p17#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p17#2/r3.claim: Listen conveys awe: Moses must ready his whole mind for a grave matter; the choice signals mercy and kindness, while the command to listen inspires fear alongside hope.
RAZI-FULL:v22p17#2/r3.anchor: يفيد نهاية الهيبة فيحصل له من الأول نهاية الرجاء

ALUSI-FULL:v16p170#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p170#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p170#2/r2.claim: One proposal takes the clause as an independent address with no syntactic governor; ma may be relative or a verbal noun, yielding listen to what is revealed or to revelation.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p170#2/r2.anchor: وقيل : هي سيف خطيب فلا متعلق لها كما ( في ردف ) لكم وما موصولة

ALUSI-FULL:v16p170#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p170#2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p170#2/r3.claim: The command to listen signals the greatness of what is revealed and the need to prepare oneself for it.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p170#2/r3.anchor: وفي أمره عليه السلام بالاستماع اشارة إلى عظم ذلك وانه يقتضى التاهب له

ALUSI-FULL:v16p170#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p170#2/r4.speaker: أبو الفضل الجوهري
ALUSI-FULL:v16p170#2/r4.claim: Abu al-Fadl al-Jawhari describes Moses standing on a stone, leaning on another, placing his right hand over his left, lowering his chin, and listening intently.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p170#2/r4.anchor: قال أبو الفضل الجوهرى : لما قيل لموسى عليه السلام استمع لما يوحى وقف على حجر واستند إلى حجر

ALUSI-FULL:v16p170#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p170#2/r5.speaker: وهب
ALUSI-FULL:v16p170#2/r5.claim: Wahb defines attentive listening as still limbs, lowered gaze, focused hearing, present understanding, and resolve to act on what God loves.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p170#2/r5.anchor: وقال وهب : أدب الاستماع سكون الجوارح وغض البصر والاصغاء بالسمع وحضور العقل والعزم على العمل

ALUSI-FULL:v16p170#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p170#2/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p170#2/r6.claim: The passive verb yuha omits its known agent; the passive also supplies the verse ending that an active form would not provide.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p170#2/r6.anchor: للعلم به ويحسنه كونه فاصله فانه لو كان مبنيا للفاعل لم يكن فاصلة

ALUSI-FULL:v16p211/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p211/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p211/r8.claim: The opening with divine choice conveys utmost kindness and the closing warning conveys overpowering severity, teaching that mercy precedes wrath and the servant must walk between hope and fear.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p211/r8.anchor: افتتح الخطاب بقوله عز قائلا ( وانا اخترتك ) وهو غاية اللطف

ALUSI-FULL:v16p211/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p211/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p211/r10.claim: Direct divine speech to Moses does not establish his superiority over Muhammad: God also addressed Muhammad directly on the Night Journey, and did so unveiled and with a vision not granted Moses.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p211/r10.anchor: والجواب أنه تعالى شأنه قد خاطب نبينا ( صلى الله عليه وسلم ) أيضا بلا واسطة ليلة المعراج

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p198/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p198/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p198/r5.claim: The verbal predication in “I chose you” strengthens the assertion rather than restricting it; the unusual, surprising news calls for reinforcement to prevent Moses from doubting it.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p198/r5.anchor: لأن المقام ليس مقام إفادة التخصيص

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p198/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p198/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p198/r6.claim: Iختيار means making an effort to seek what is good; the effort form here is used for excellent pursuit of good.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p198/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p198/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p198/r7.claim: The command to listen to revelation follows from being chosen: the choice means selecting Moses to receive what God will reveal.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p198/r7.anchor: وفرع على الإخبار باختياره أن أمر بالاستماع للوحي لأنه أثر الاختيار إذ لا معنى للاختيار إلا اختياره لتلقي ما سيوحي الله

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p198/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p198/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p198/r8.claim: The immediate command concerns the revelation being delivered then; Moses' duty to listen to future revelations is understood a fortiori.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p198/r8.anchor: ما يوحى إليه حينئذ من الكلام

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p198/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p198/r9.speaker: حمزة
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p198/r9.claim: Ḥamza alone reads “We chose you,” using the pronoun of majesty.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p198/r9.anchor: حمزة وحده { وأنا اخترناك بضميري التعظيم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p198/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p198/r10.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p198/r10.claim: The lām in “for what is revealed” strengthens the transitive link from istamiʿ to its object.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p198/r10.anchor: للتقوية في تعدية فعل ( استمع ) إلى مفعوله

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p198/r11.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p198/r11.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p198/r11.claim: Alternatively, the lām may depend on “I chose you,” meaning “I chose you for revelation, so listen,” with the intervening clause parenthetical.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p198/r12.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p198/r12.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p198/r12.claim: Alternatively, istamiʿ may carry the sense of aṣghi, “listen attentively.”
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p198/r12.anchor: ويجوز أن يضمن استمع معنى أصغغ

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p203/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p203/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p203/r4.claim: The address reasons through each command and prohibition: identify God and His oneness, derive worship and prayer, affirm the Hour and its requital, warn against deniers, and show that violating the warning brings ruin.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p203/r4.anchor: فابتدىء بالإعلام بأن الذي يكلمه هو الله ، وأنه لا إله إلا هو
